title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a computational fragment from a case analysis (part c) begins with 'd<0', so parts a) and b) presumably treat d>0 and d=0) of graded Hom-modules between objects of the form M_{S_h}. The most plausible reading is M_{S_h} = M ⊗ S_h, where S_h is a divided-power polynomial algebra in a variable T (possibly truncated, or taken over a base like Z/p^h). This algebra has basis T^{(j)}. τ_α is the 'truncation' submodule spanned by m T^{(j)} with j ≥ α.

(1) Degree-d maps into a smaller truncation. A degree-d map τ_α M_{S_h} → τ_β N_{S_h} is the same as a degree-d map into τ_{α+d} N_{S_h} whose image lies in the submodule τ_β N_{S_h} ⊂ τ_{α+d} N_{S_h}. Grothendieck tentatively identifies these maps, with a question mark, with Hom_h(M,N), presumably maps of the underlying modules over the level-h base.

(2) The explicit formula. Such a map is m T^{(j)} ↦ c_{d,j} u(m) T^{(d+j)} for some u: M → N. The constants c_{d,j} are presumably the divided-power structure constants, since T^{(d)}T^{(j)} = binom(d+j, j) T^{(d+j)}. They could also be the constants of a differential-operator action.

(3) The condition. The image lands in τ_β exactly when the coefficient of every T^{(d+j)} with d+j < β vanishes, that is, c_{d,j} u = 0 for α ≤ j < β−d. So the sub-Hom is cut out by a family of torsion conditions on u. This is the kind of computation that arises with divided powers in mixed characteristic, where binomial coefficients are not units.

(4) Case d<0. Grothendieck notes that N^*_{S_h} = φ_{0β} τ_β N_{S_h} = τ_0 φ^*_{ββ} N_{S_h}, which is contained in φ_β N_{S_h}. Here φ seems to be a shift or re-indexing (Frobenius-like or 'twist') operation. Hence, for M^* in the subcategory ℳ^*, there is an inclusion Hom^d(M^*, N_{S_h}) ⊂ Hom^d(M^*, φ^*_{ββ} N_{S_h}). He then identifies the right side with Hom(M^*[−d], φ_β N_{S_h}) = Hom_β(M^*[−d], N_{S_h}), trading a degree shift for a twisted Hom. The page breaks off there.

The whole page is routine bookkeeping for computing Hom (or Ext) groups in a category of graded modules over a divided-power de Rham-type algebra. This presumably serves the Hodge/de Rham–crystalline comparison theme of the 1976 IHÉS lecture.
errors: Off-by-one inconsistency. The displayed system runs up to c_{d,β−d}u = 0, but the summary condition reads α ≤ j < β−d. Image in τ_β requires vanishing exactly for d+j < β, i.e. j ≤ β−d−1. The strict inequality is correct, so the last line of the system should be c_{d,β−d−1}u = 0. Grothendieck visibly corrected that subscript, so he may have hesitated over it.

The identification of the sub-Hom with Hom_h(M,N) is marked with '?'. It is in any case only correct after imposing the vanishing conditions, i.e. the sub-Hom is the submodule of Hom_h(M,N) killed by the c_{d,j}, not all of it.

In part c) the notation φ_{0β}, φ^*_{ββ}, φ_β is not defined on this page, so the claimed equalities cannot be checked from the page alone. The middle equality Hom^d(M^*, φ^*_{ββ}N) = Hom(M^*[−d], φ_β N) silently changes φ^*_{ββ} to φ_β.

ideas.what: Degree-d maps between truncations of divided-power modules described by a module map u and divided-power binomial constants, with the condition that the image lies in a deeper truncation expressed as c_{d,j}u = 0
ideas.modern_name: Hom computations for graded modules over the divided-power algebra / filtered modules with divided-power filtration (cf. crystalline filtrations, Fontaine–Laffaille-type modules)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Divided-power de Rham theory: Berthelot, Illusie, Mazur–Ogus (1970s); filtered modules: Fontaine–Laffaille (1982)
ideas.where_published: The 1976 IHÉS lecture is not known to me in published form

ideas.what: Trading a degree-d (d<0) Hom for a degree-0 Hom into a twisted/shifted object, Hom^d(M^*,N) ⊂ Hom(M^*[−d], φ_β N) = Hom_β(M^*[−d],N)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine graded-Hom bookkeeping with divided-power binomial constants. The case analysis is fragmentary and the notation (φ, ℳ^*, S_h) is undefined here, so no new result or connection is identifiable from this page alone.
transcription_corrections: In the top-right Hom the crossed-out subscript was replaced; the target is τ_β N_{S_h} in the first expression on the line, and τ_{α+d} N_{S_h} in the second.
The last equation of the system reads c_{d,β−d}u = 0, with the subscript visibly overwritten.
In the summary line, after 'α ≤ j < β−d' there is a crossed-out alternative bound, so the '[-...-]' in the transcription is a deletion.
In part c), the superscript on φ^*_{ββ} is uncertain; it may read φ_{ββ}^{*} or φ_{β}^{*}.
